criteria.evidence: All five guided sections are present and substantive: 'It runs over the shop's abandoned-cart, reminder and order records whenever new records arrive, and once more when a month's window has passed to close that month. It produces one match record per abandoned cart...'; inputs and outputs name each field; 11 rules cover branches; 8 Given/When/Then criteria; 4 out-of-scope items each naming an owner.

'Matching on the cart id, not on the shopper, keeps the rule exact and free of personal data; a shopper who starts a fresh cart instead is not counted, which undercounts slightly but never overcounts.' and 'A reminder sent after the order does not turn an unprompted return into a reminded one, because that would credit reminders with sales they did not cause.'

Rules are discrete bullets; acceptance is Given/When/Then: 'Given a matched order partly refunded after its month is final, when the refund arrives, then the closed month's figure is unchanged and a dated correction with the refunded amount is recorded against that month.' The functionality states behavior, not a user story.

Parent lists only: 'Won-back order matching (won-back-order-matching) — decides for each abandoned cart whether it ended in an order within the win-back window... and its net value'. The child adds the exact input fields, outcome set, one-to-one matching, last-reminder handling, month-closing and correction behavior, and testable criteria.

'It produces one match record per abandoned cart, which is the only definition of "a cart won back" that the baseline, the owner's view and the business summary are allowed to use'; Out of scope names the neighbours: 'Pre-reminder baseline owns that, using these match records.'
